title_ur: انتخابِ اکبر: پیش رو یعنی قطعات
author: Akbar Allahabadi
edition: Kulliyat-e-Akbar, Part 1, 4th edition, Standard Press, Allahabad, 1914: the section Pesh-rau (pp. 157-196), 60 pieces; 6 unreadable pieces are left out.
description: Akbar Allahabadi (1846–1921), judge, wit and the great comic poet of Urdu, wrote the sharpest verse commentary on India's meeting with the West: on the "New Light" of English education, English clothes and words, Sir Sayyid and the Aligarh college, Westernised young men and their English brides, purdah, the railway and the telegraph, and the Viceroy's durbars. This book gives the complete section "Pesh-rau" ("The Vanguard") of his collected poems, sixty pieces including "A Glimpse of the Delhi Durbar", "Lightning in the Church", the purdah poem of 1891, his answer to Southey's "Cataract of Lodore", "The Curzon Sabha" and the national poem written for Mohsin-ul-Mulk, with his parodies of Hafiz and Sa'di. Urdu text from Kulliyat-e-Akbar, Part One (4th ed., Standard Press, Allahabad, 1914), with a facing line-by-line English translation, notes on the puns and Persian quotations, an introduction and a glossary. A core text for courses on Urdu poetry and on colonialism and modernity in South Asia.
translation_note: Faithful English translation made for this library, section by section, with translator's notes marked [TN]. Each reading section is one chapter, ending with a glossary.
